title: 8-round AES-192: Impossible differential, medium-data endpoint

target.description: Standard AES-192 under the paper's round numbering: initial whitening k0, rounds1 onward; last MixColumns omitted for 8-round recovery variants. Guess10 bytes0,1,4,7,10,11,12,13,14,15 of k8 and byte3 of w7, then recover8 whitening bytes:152 bits of named subkey material. These are selected round-key values, not an independently priced complete192-bit master key.

setting.key_relation: Two unknown AES-192 master keys K and K'=K XOR Delta, where Delta[0]=Delta[8]=a!=0 and the other22 bytes are0. Initial whitening is k0; round subkeys are k1,... .
setting.key_population: General unknown key pair with attacker-chosen nonzero a; b,c are actual key-dependent S-box output differences, not independently chosen subkeys.
setting.plaintext_model: One structure has two pools of2^64 inputs, giving2^128 cross-key pairs using2^65 queries.2^23 structures and a2^-80 filter give2^71 retained pairs.
assumptions: The source models pair filters and incorrect whitening-key eliminations probabilistically; those independence assumptions have not been proved for every AES key.
Named subkey bits may be dependent. No complete192-bit master-key recovery budget is supplied.
The source uses64 memory accesses per encryption equivalent; this is an accounting convention, not an independent implementation measurement.
The88-bit terminal guess computes b,c; total2^88 data counts both keys and all structures.

time.note: Source formula uses2^71 retained pairs,2^88 terminal hypotheses, a2^-6 memory-access conversion. Remaining master-key completion is not priced.

data.note: Total plaintext-block encryption queries across exactly2 related keys, not a per-key budget.

success.description: No numerical recovery success is supplied for this 152-bit named-subkey output.
